content.value_statement: Teams need to assess EU accessibility obligations and organize testing evidence. This guide frames scope assessment, WCAG review planning, remediation priorities, and draft accessibility statements.
actual_capabilities: Outlines EAA scope considerations, including service categories, product rules, micro-enterprise exemptions, and disproportionate burden.
Defines WCAG 2.1 A and AA as the intended audit coverage.
Identifies keyboard, screen reader, zoom, reflow, and automated scanning as testing areas.
Describes prioritized remediation reports and illustrates a keyboard accessibility finding with a suggested fix.
Frames draft accessibility statements with feedback mechanisms and enforcement contacts.
limitations: The supplied folder contains only a public guide, without the original scripts, extension source, or templates.
The guide does not include detailed procedures for every WCAG success criterion or a complete reusable checklist.
Actual findings require website access, suitable testing tools, and manual verification.
Draft statements and scope assessments require legal review and do not certify compliance.

use_cases.title: Assess an online shop
use_cases.description: Organize business facts and unresolved questions for an EAA scope memo before commissioning a detailed audit.

use_cases.title: Plan checkout accessibility testing
use_cases.description: Structure keyboard, screen reader, zoom, and reflow checks, then turn verified findings into remediation priorities.

use_cases.title: Prepare a draft accessibility statement
use_cases.description: Summarize tested coverage, known barriers, feedback channels, and enforcement contacts for legal review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a scope assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Help assess EAA scope for my business: [country, service, employee count, turnover]. Ask for missing facts and distinguish assumptions from conclusions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: gather business facts before planning an audit.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a focused review
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a WCAG 2.1 AA review of [checkout flow]. Include keyboard, screen reader, zoom, and reflow checks. Mark all untested criteria explicitly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: organize testing for one customer journey.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize verified barriers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these verified findings: [evidence]. Draft a remediation report with affected steps, relevant WCAG criteria, user impact, suggested fixes, and retest requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: convert testing evidence into engineering work.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare review documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [business facts], [audit evidence], and [contact details], draft a scope memo and accessibility statement. Separate verified results, assumptions, exemptions, and legal questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: prepare evidence-linked documents for specialist review.

output_examples.input: Our German webshop has 15 employees and EUR 3 million turnover. Help prepare an EAA scope assessment.
output: Preliminary scope: the stated employee count does not meet the micro-enterprise definition.
Confirm the covered service category, applicable national rules, and any transitional provisions before finalizing the memo.
Next step: document the checkout journey and gather accessibility testing evidence.

output_examples.input: Testing confirmed that the checkout payment control cannot be activated using a keyboard. Draft a remediation finding.
output: Finding: keyboard users cannot complete payment. Relevant criterion: WCAG 2.1.1, Keyboard.
Priority: high because the barrier blocks checkout completion.
Suggested fix: use a native button with an accessible name and working keyboard activation.
Retest: verify focus order, visible focus, and activation with Enter and Space.

best_practices: Record tested pages, user journeys, environments, and evidence before drafting findings.
Combine automated checks with manual keyboard, screen reader, zoom, and reflow testing.
Have qualified reviewers verify legal scope, exemption claims, and accessibility statements before publication.
anti_patterns: Treating an AI-generated statement as proof of legal compliance.
Claiming all WCAG criteria pass after automated scanning alone.
Assuming the public guide includes executable audit tools or the original package templates.

faq.question: Does this package automatically scan my website?
faq.answer: No scanning software is included. The public guide describes an audit approach; execution depends on your agent, available tools, and manual testing.

faq.question: Which accessibility standard does the guide target?
faq.answer: It targets WCAG 2.1 A and AA within an EAA review context and discusses accessibility statements associated with EN 301 549.

faq.question: Can it determine whether the EAA applies to my business?
faq.answer: It outlines relevant scope questions. A reliable conclusion requires business facts, applicable national rules, and qualified legal review.

faq.question: Are scripts and templates included?
faq.answer: No. The supplied file explicitly excludes the original scripts, extension source, and templates.

faq.question: Can I publish the generated accessibility statement directly?
faq.answer: Treat it as a draft. Verify every claim against testing evidence and have counsel review applicable legal requirements.

faq.question: Can I use the guide after fixing accessibility issues?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to organize retesting, update verified findings, and revise the statement to reflect current evidence.
